name: Hemoglobin
measures: the protein in red blood cells that carries oxygen around the body.
low: iron, vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, blood loss, or long-term illness.
high: dehydration, living at high altitude, smoking, or some lung and bone-marrow conditions.

name: RBC
measures: the number of red blood cells, which carry oxygen.
low: anemia from nutrient deficiency, blood loss or chronic disease.
high: dehydration, high altitude, smoking or lung disease.

name: MCV
measures: the average size of your red blood cells.
low: small red cells, often with iron deficiency.
high: large red cells, often with vitamin B12 or folate deficiency, alcohol use or thyroid problems.

name: WBC
measures: the number of white blood cells, which fight infection.
low: viral infections, some medicines, or bone-marrow and immune conditions.
high: infection, inflammation, stress, smoking or some medicines.

name: Platelets
measures: tiny cell pieces that help blood clot.
low: viral infections, some medicines, immune conditions or bone-marrow problems.
high: iron deficiency, infection, inflammation or recovery from illness.

name: Glucose
measures: the amount of sugar in your blood.
low: skipping meals, some diabetes medicines, or hormone problems.
high: eating before a fasting test, stress, infection, or diabetes or pre-diabetes.

name: HbA1c
measures: your average blood sugar over about the last three months.
low: recent blood loss, some anemias, or frequent very low sugar levels.
high: blood sugar that has been running above normal over the past months.

name: Total Cholesterol
measures: the total amount of cholesterol, a fatty substance, in your blood.
low: a very low-fat diet, an overactive thyroid, or liver problems.
high: a diet high in saturated fat, little exercise, family history, or thyroid and kidney conditions.

name: LDL Cholesterol
measures: cholesterol carried in LDL particles, often called bad cholesterol.
low: usually not a concern; sometimes caused by medicines or other conditions.
high: diet, weight, little exercise, family history or an underactive thyroid.

name: HDL Cholesterol
measures: cholesterol carried in HDL particles, often called good cholesterol.
low: smoking, being overweight, little exercise or diabetes.
high: usually a good sign; sometimes from genetics or high alcohol intake.

name: Triglycerides
measures: a type of fat in the blood that comes from food and the liver.
low: usually not a concern.
high: sugary or fatty foods, alcohol, being overweight, diabetes, or not fasting before the test.

name: Creatinine
measures: a waste product from muscles that the kidneys filter out.
low: low muscle mass or pregnancy.
high: reduced kidney function, dehydration, a high-protein meal, or heavy muscle mass.

name: Urea
measures: a waste product of protein breakdown that the kidneys remove.
low: low protein intake, liver problems or drinking a lot of water.
high: dehydration, a high-protein diet, or reduced kidney function.

name: Uric Acid
measures: a waste product from breaking down purines found in some foods and body cells.
low: some medicines or kidney conditions.
high: a diet rich in purines, alcohol, reduced kidney function, or a tendency toward gout.

name: ALT
measures: an enzyme found mostly in the liver that leaks into the blood when liver cells are irritated.
low: usually not a concern.
high: fatty liver, alcohol, some medicines, viral infections of the liver or other liver irritation.

name: AST
measures: an enzyme found in the liver, heart and muscles.
low: usually not a concern.
high: liver irritation, intense exercise, muscle injury or some medicines.

name: Bilirubin
measures: a yellow substance made when old red blood cells break down and cleared by the liver.
low: usually not a concern.
high: liver or bile-duct problems, faster red cell breakdown, or a harmless inherited tendency.

name: Albumin
measures: the main protein in the blood, made by the liver.
low: liver or kidney problems, poor nutrition or long-term inflammation.
high: usually from dehydration.

name: TSH
measures: a hormone from the brain that tells the thyroid how much hormone to make.
low: often goes with an overactive thyroid, or some medicines.
high: often goes with an underactive thyroid.

name: Vitamin D
measures: the level of vitamin D, which helps the body absorb calcium for bones.
low: little sun exposure, diet, darker skin, or absorption problems.
high: usually from taking too many supplements.

name: Vitamin B12
measures: a vitamin needed for healthy nerves and for making red blood cells.
low: a diet low in animal foods, absorption problems, or some medicines.
high: often from supplements or injections.

name: Sodium
measures: a mineral that balances water in your body.
low: too much water, some medicines, or vomiting and diarrhea.
high: not drinking enough water or fluid loss.

name: Potassium
measures: a mineral that helps nerves and muscles, including the heart, work.
low: vomiting, diarrhea or some water tablets.
high: kidney problems, some medicines, or a damaged blood sample.

name: CRP
measures: a protein the liver makes when there is inflammation.
low: this is the expected range.
high: infection, injury or other inflammation.

name: Ferritin
measures: the amount of iron your body has stored.
low: low iron stores, often from diet or blood loss.
high: inflammation, liver conditions, or too much iron.
